sanskrit: tatas tasmin pranṛtte vai sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca yat pranṛttam ubhayaṃ vīra tejasā tasya mohitam
english: Then, as he danced, O hero, whatever was immovable and whatever was moving — both were bewildered by his blazing energy as he danced.

sanskrit: brahmādibhiḥ surai rājann ṛṣibhiś ca tapodhanaiḥ vijñapto vai mahādeva ṛṣer arthe narādhipa nāyaṃ nṛtyed yathā deva tathā tvaṃ kartum arhasi
english: The gods headed by Brahma and the sages rich in austerities petitioned Mahadeva, O king, on behalf of the sage, O lord of men: 'This one should not dance thus; O god, it is fitting that you act accordingly.'

sanskrit: tataḥ pranṛttam āsādya harṣāviṣṭena cetasā surāṇāṃ hitakāmārtham ṛṣiṃ devo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Then, approaching the one who was dancing, his mind filled with joy, the god, desiring the welfare of the gods, spoke to the sage.

sanskrit: aho maharṣe dharmajña kimarthaṃ nṛtyate bhavān harṣasthānaṃ kimarthaṃ vā tavādya munipuṃgava
english: 'Ah, O great sage, O knower of dharma, why do you dance? What is your occasion for rejoicing today, O best among sages?'

sanskrit: ṛṣir uvāca kiṃ na paśyasi me deva karāc chākarasaṃ srutam yaṃ dṛṣṭvāhaṃ pranṛtto vai harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ
english: The sage said: 'Do you not see, O god, the drop of Śākara's essence that has flowed from my hand? Having seen it I have danced, filled with great joy.'

sanskrit: pulastya uvāca taṃ prahasyābravīd devo muniṃ rāgeṇa mohitam ahaṃ vai vismayaṃ vipra na gacchāmīti paśya mām
english: Pulastya said: Laughing, the god spoke to the sage who was deluded by passion: 'I, O brahmin, am not amazed — look at me.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā naraśreṣṭha mahādevena dhīmatā aṅgulyagreṇa rājendra svāṅguṣṭhas tāḍito 'nagha
english: Having spoken thus, O best of men, by the wise Mahadeva, with the tip of his finger, O lord of kings, his own thumb was struck, O sinless one.

sanskrit: tato bhasma kṣatād rājan nirgataṃ himasaṃnibham tad dṛṣṭvā vrīḍito rājan sa muniḥ pādayor gataḥ
english: Then ashes, white as snow, emerged from the wound, O king. Seeing this, the sage, ashamed, O king, fell at his feet.

sanskrit: nānyaṃ devam ahaṃ manye rudrāt parataraṃ mahat surāsurasya jagato gatis tvam asi śūladhṛk
english: 'I regard no other god as greater than Rudra. You are the refuge of the world of gods and demons, O bearer of the trident.'

sanskrit: tvayā sṛṣṭam idaṃ viśvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram tvām eva bhagavan sarve praviśanti yugakṣaye
english: 'This universe, the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings, was created by you; at the end of the age, O blessed lord, all enter into you alone.'

sanskrit: devair api na śakyas tvaṃ parijñātuṃ kuto mayā tvayi sarve ca dṛśyante surā brahmādayo 'nagha
english: 'You cannot be fully known even by the gods — how then by me? All the gods, with Brahma at their head, are seen in you, O sinless one.'

sanskrit: sarvas tvam asi lokānāṃ kartā kārayitā ca ha tvatprasādāt surāḥ sarve modantīhākutobhayāḥ evaṃ stutvā mahādevaṃ sa ṛṣiḥ praṇato 'bhavat
english: 'You are the all, the maker and the cause of all worlds; by your grace all gods here rejoice, fearless. Having thus praised Mahadeva, the sage bowed low.

sanskrit: ṛṣir uvāca tvatprasādān mahādeva tapo me na kṣareta vai
english: The sage said: 'By your grace, O Mahadeva, my austerity shall not be diminished.'

sanskrit: pulastya uvāca tato devaḥ prahṛṣṭātmā brahmarṣim idam abravīt tapas te vardhatāṃ vipra matprasādāt sahasradhā
english: Pulastya said: Then the god, his heart delighted, spoke these words to the brahmin-sage: 'O brahmin, may your austerity increase a thousandfold by my grace.'

sanskrit: āśrame ceha vatsyāmi tvayā sārdhaṃ mahāmune saptasārasvate snātvā arcayiṣyanti ye tu mām
english: 'And here in this hermitage I shall dwell together with you, O great sage. Those who bathe at the Saptasārasvata and worship me —'

sanskrit: na teṣāṃ durlabhaṃ kiṃ cid iha loke paratra ca sārasvataṃ ca te lokaṃ gamiṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ
english: '— nothing shall be unattainable for them in this world or the next, and they shall go to the world of Sarasvata — there is no doubt.'

sanskrit: tatas tv auśanasaṃ gacchet triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam yatra brahmādayo devā ṛṣayaś ca tapodhanāḥ
english: Then one should go to Auśanasa, celebrated in the three worlds, where the gods headed by Brahma and the sages rich in austerity —

sanskrit: kārttikeyaś ca bhagavāṃs trisaṃdhyaṃ kila bhārata sāṃnidhyam akarot tatra bhārgavapriyakāmyayā
english: — and the blessed Kārttikeya, at the three junctions of the day, O Bhārata, made his presence there, desiring to please Bhārgava.

sanskrit: kapālamocanaṃ tīrthaṃ sarvapāpapramocanam tatra snātvā naravyāghra sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: The tīrtha Kapālamocana releases one from all sins; bathing there, O tiger among men, one is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: agnitīrthaṃ tato gacchet tatra snātvā nararṣabha agnilokam avāpnoti kulaṃ caiva samuddharet
english: Then one should go to Agnitīrtha; having bathed there, O bull among men, one attains the world of Agni and also redeems one's family.

sanskrit: viśvāmitrasya tatraiva tīrthaṃ bharatasattama tatra snātvā mahārāja brāhmaṇyam abhijāyate
english: There too is the tīrtha of Viśvāmitra, O best of the Bharatas; having bathed there, O great king, one is reborn into brahminhood.

sanskrit: brahmayoniṃ samāsādya śuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ tatra snātvā naravyāghra brahmalokaṃ prapadyate punāty āsaptamaṃ caiva kulaṃ nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: Reaching Brahmayoni, pure and with a collected mind, and bathing there, O tiger among men, one attains the world of Brahma and purifies one's family to the seventh generation — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam pṛthūdakam iti khyātaṃ kārttikeyasya vai nṛpa tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvīta pitṛdevārcane rataḥ
english: Then one should go, O lord of kings, to the tīrtha celebrated in the three worlds, known as Pṛthūdaka, O king, belonging to Kārttikeya; one should perform ablutions there, devoted to the worship of ancestors and gods.

sanskrit: ajñānāj jñānato vāpi striyā vā puruṣeṇa vā yat kiṃ cid aśubhaṃ karma kṛtaṃ mānuṣabuddhinā
english: Whatever inauspicious act has been done out of ignorance or knowledge, by a woman or a man, with human understanding —

sanskrit: tat sarvaṃ naśyate tasya snātamātrasya bhārata aśvamedhaphalaṃ cāpi svargalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: — all of that perishes for one who has merely bathed there, O Bhārata, and one also gains the fruit of the Aśvamedha and goes to the heavenly world.

sanskrit: puṇyam āhuḥ kurukṣetraṃ kurukṣetrāt sarasvatīm sarasvatyāś ca tīrthāni tīrthebhyaś ca pṛthūdakam
english: They say Kurukṣetra is holy; holier than Kurukṣetra is Sarasvatī; holier than Sarasvatī are the tīrthas; and holiest among the tīrthas is Pṛthūdaka.

sanskrit: uttame sarvatīrthānāṃ yas tyajed ātmanas tanum pṛthūdake japyaparo nainaṃ śvomaraṇaṃ tapet
english: One who, at the best of all tīrthas, gives up his body at Pṛthūdaka, devoted to silent prayer, will not grieve at tomorrow's death.

sanskrit: gītaṃ sanatkumāreṇa vyāsena ca mahātmanā vede ca niyataṃ rājan abhigacchet pṛthūdakam
english: It is declared by Sanatkumāra and by the great-souled Vyāsa, and is fixed in the Veda, O king — one should go to Pṛthūdaka.

sanskrit: pṛthūdakāt puṇyatamaṃ nānyat tīrthaṃ narottama etan medhyaṃ pavitraṃ ca pāvanaṃ ca na saṃśayaḥ
english: There is no tīrtha more holy than Pṛthūdaka, O best of men; this is pure, sacred, and purifying — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tatra snātvā divaṃ yānti api pāpakṛto janāḥ pṛthūdake naraśreṣṭha prāhur evaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Even those who have committed sins go to heaven after bathing there, O best of men at Pṛthūdaka — so the wise declare.

sanskrit: madhusravaṃ ca tatraiva tīrthaṃ bharatasattama tatra snātvā naro rājan gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: And there too is the tīrtha Madhusrava, O best of the Bharatas; a man who bathes there, O king, obtains the merit of giving a thousand cows.

sanskrit: tato gacchet naraśreṣṭha tīrthaṃ devyā yathākramam sarasvatyāruṇāyāś ca saṃgamaṃ lokaviśrutam
english: Then one should go in order, O best of men, to the tīrtha of the goddess — the confluence of Sarasvatī and Aruṇā, celebrated throughout the world.

sanskrit: trirātropoṣitaḥ snātvā mucyate brahmahatyayā agniṣṭomātirātrābhyāṃ phalaṃ vindati mānavaḥ
english: Fasting for three nights and bathing, one is freed from the sin of killing a brahmin, and a man gains the merit of Agniṣṭoma and Atirātra sacrifices.

sanskrit: āsaptamaṃ kulaṃ caiva punāti bharatarṣabha avatīrṇaṃ ca tatraiva tīrthaṃ kurukulodvaha viprāṇām anukampārthaṃ darbhiṇā nirmitaṃ purā
english: And one purifies one's family to the seventh generation, O bull of the Bharatas. There too is the tīrtha Avatīrṇa, O chief of the Kuru lineage, formerly created by Darbhiṇa out of compassion for the brahmins.

sanskrit: vratopanayanābhyāṃ vā upavāsena vā dvijaḥ kriyāmantraiś ca saṃyukto brāhmaṇaḥ syān na saṃśayaḥ
english: A twice-born, whether through vow and sacred thread ceremony or through fasting, accompanied by rites and mantras, shall become a true brahmin — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: kriyāmantravihīno 'pi tatra snātvā nararṣabha cīrṇavrato bhaved vipro dṛṣṭam etat purātane
english: Even one destitute of rites and mantras, having bathed there, O bull among men, shall become a brahmin who has fulfilled his vows — this has been seen in ancient tradition.

sanskrit: samudrāś cāpi catvāraḥ samānītāś ca darbhiṇā yeṣu snāto naravyāghra na durgatim avāpnuyāt phalāni gosahasrāṇāṃ caturṇāṃ vindate ca saḥ
english: The four oceans were also brought together there by Darbhiṇa; one who has bathed in them, O tiger among men, shall not attain an evil end, and he gains the merit of four thousand cows.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra tīrthaṃ śatasahasrakam sāhasrakaṃ ca tatraiva dve tīrthe lokaviśrute
english: Then one should go, O lord of kings, to the tīrtha Śatasāhasraka; and there too is Sāhasraka — two tīrthas celebrated throughout the world.

sanskrit: ubhayor hi naraḥ snātvā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet dānaṃ vāpy upavāso vā sahasraguṇitaṃ bhavet
english: For a man who bathes in both obtains the merit of a thousand cows, and any gift or fast done there becomes a thousandfold in merit.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra reṇukātīrtham uttamam tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvīta pitṛdevārcane rataḥ sravapāpaviśuddhātmā agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: Then one should go, O lord of kings, to the excellent tīrtha of Reṇukā; one should perform ablutions there, devoted to the worship of ancestors and gods; with a soul purified of all sins, one obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit: vimocanam upaspṛśya jitamanyur jitendriyaḥ pratigrahakṛtair doṣaiḥ sarvaiḥ sa parimucyate
english: Touching the waters of Vimocana, with anger conquered and senses mastered, one is freed from all the faults incurred by accepting gifts.

sanskrit: tataḥ pañcavaṭaṃ gatvā brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ puṇyena mahatā yuktaḥ satāṃ loke mahīyate
english: Then, going to Pañcavaṭa as a celibate with senses mastered, endowed with great merit, one is honoured in the world of the righteous.

sanskrit: yatra yogeśvaraḥ sthāṇuḥ svayam eva vṛṣadhvajaḥ tam arcayitvā deveśaṃ gamanād eva sidhyati
english: There the lord of yoga, Sthāṇu himself, whose banner is the bull — having worshipped that lord of gods, one attains perfection by going there alone.

sanskrit: aujasaṃ varuṇaṃ tīrthaṃ dīpyate svena tejasā yatra brahmādibhir devair ṛṣibhiś ca tapodhanaiḥ senāpatyena devānām abhiṣikto guhas tadā
english: The tīrtha of Varuṇa at Aujasa blazes with its own splendour; there Guha was consecrated as the commander-in-chief of the gods by the gods headed by Brahma and by the sages rich in austerities.

sanskrit: aujasasya tu pūrveṇa kurutīrthaṃ kurūdvaha kurutīrthe naraḥ snātvā brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā kurulokaṃ prapadyate
english: To the east of Aujasa is Kurutīrtha, O chief of the Kurus; a man who bathes at Kurutīrtha, a celibate with senses mastered and soul purified of all sins, attains the world of the Kurus.

sanskrit: svargadvāraṃ tato gacchen niyato niyatāśanaḥ svargalokam avāpnoti brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Then one should go to Svargadvāra with discipline and regulated diet; one attains the heavenly world and also goes to the world of Brahma.

sanskrit: tato gacched anarakaṃ tīrthasevī narādhipa tatra snātvā naro rājan na durgatim avāpnuyāt
english: Then one who frequents tīrthas should go to Anaraka, O lord of men; a man who bathes there, O king, shall not attain an evil end.

sanskrit: tatra brahmā svayaṃ nityaṃ devaiḥ saha mahīpate anvāsyate naraśreṣṭha nārāyaṇapurogamaiḥ
english: There Brahma himself is ever attended, O lord of the earth, O best of men, by the gods led by Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: sāṃnidhyaṃ caiva rājendra rudrapatnyāḥ kurūdvaha abhigamya ca tāṃ devīṃ na durgatim avāpnuyāt
english: And the presence of Rudra's consort is there, O lord of kings, O chief of the Kurus; having approached that goddess, one shall not attain an evil end.

sanskrit: tatraiva ca mahārāja viśveśvaram umāpatim abhigamya mahādevaṃ mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ
english: And there too, O great king, by approaching Viśveśvara, the husband of Umā, the great god, one is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇaṃ cābhigamya padmanābham ariṃdamam śobhamāno mahārāja viṣṇulokaṃ prapadyate
english: And by approaching Nārāyaṇa of the lotus-navel, the subduer of enemies, one shines forth, O great king, and attains the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tīrthe tu sarvadevānāṃ snātaḥ sa puruṣarṣabha sarvaduḥkhaiḥ parityakto dyotate śaśivat sadā
english: But one who has bathed at the tīrtha of all the gods, O bull among men, having abandoned all sorrows, shines forever like the moon.

sanskrit: tataḥ svastipuraṃ gacchet tīrthasevī narādhipa pāvanaṃ tīrtham āsādya tarpayet pitṛdevatāḥ agniṣṭomasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: Then a frequenter of tīrthas should go to Svastipura, O lord of men; reaching this purifying tīrtha and satisfying the ancestors and gods, a man obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit: gaṅgāhradaś ca tatraiva kūpaś ca bharatarṣabha tisraḥ koṭyas tu tīrthānāṃ tasmin kūpe mahīpate tatra snātvā naro rājan svargalokaṃ prapadyate
english: And there too is a pool of the Gaṅgā and a well, O bull of the Bharatas; three crores of tīrthas are in that well, O lord of the earth; a man who bathes there, O king, attains the heavenly world.

sanskrit: āpagāyāṃ naraḥ snātvā arcayitvā maheśvaram gāṇapatyam avāpnoti kulaṃ coddharate svakam
english: A man who bathes in the Āpagā river and worships Maheśvara attains a place among the hosts of Gaṇa and also redeems his own family.

sanskrit: tataḥ sthāṇuvaṭaṃ gacchet triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam tatra snātvā sthito rātriṃ rudralokam avāpnuyāt
english: Then one should go to Sthāṇuvaṭa, celebrated in the three worlds; having bathed there and stayed the night, one would attain the world of Rudra.

sanskrit: badarīpācanaṃ gacched vasiṣṭhasyāśramaṃ tataḥ badaraṃ bhakṣayet tatra trirātropoṣito naraḥ
english: One should go to Badarīpācana, then to the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha; a man should eat the jujube fruit there, having fasted for three nights.

sanskrit: samyag dvādaśa varṣāṇi badarān bhakṣayet tu yaḥ trirātropoṣitaś caiva bhavet tulyo narādhipa
english: One who properly eats the jujube fruit for twelve full years, as well as one who fasts for three nights, shall be equal in merit, O lord of men.

sanskrit: indramārgaṃ samāsādya tīrthasevī narādhipa ahorātropavāsena śakraloke mahīyate
english: Reaching Indramārga, a frequenter of tīrthas, O lord of men, is honoured in the world of Śakra by fasting for a day and a night.

sanskrit: ekarātraṃ samāsādya ekarātroṣito naraḥ niyataḥ satyavādī ca brahmaloke mahīyate
english: Staying for one night, a man who has remained there for a single night, disciplined and truthful in speech, is honoured in the world of Brahma.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam ādityasyāśramo yatra tejorāśer mahātmanaḥ
english: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the tīrtha celebrated in the three worlds, where is the hermitage of Āditya, that great-souled mass of radiance.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tīrthe naraḥ snātvā pūjayitvā vibhāvasum ādityalokaṃ vrajati kulaṃ caiva samuddharet
english: A man who bathes at that tīrtha and worships Vibhāvasu goes to the world of Āditya and also redeems his family.

sanskrit: somatīrthe naraḥ snātvā tīrthasevī kurūdvaha somalokam avāpnoti naro nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: A man who bathes at Somatīrtha, a frequenter of tīrthas, O chief of the Kurus, attains the world of Soma — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña dadhīcasya mahātmanaḥ tīrthaṃ puṇyatamaṃ rājan pāvanaṃ lokaviśrutam
english: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the most holy tīrtha of the great-souled Dadhīca, O king — purifying and celebrated throughout the world.

sanskrit: yatra sārasvato rājan so 'ṅgirās tapaso nidhiḥ tasmiṃs tīrthe naraḥ snātvā vājapeyaphalaṃ labhet sārasvatīṃ gatiṃ caiva labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Where, O king, that Sārasvata, that Āṅgirasa, that treasury of austerity dwells — a man who bathes at that tīrtha obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice and also attains the state of Sārasvata — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tataḥ kanyāśramaṃ gacchen niyato brahmacaryavān trirātropoṣito rājann upavāsaparāyaṇaḥ labhet kanyāśataṃ divyaṃ brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Then one should go to Kanyāśrama, disciplined and celibate, fasting for three nights, O king, devoted to fasting; one obtains a hundred divine maidens and goes to the world of Brahma.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña tīrthaṃ saṃnihitīm api yatra brahmādayo devā ṛṣayaś ca tapodhanāḥ māsi māsi samāyānti puṇyena mahatānvitāḥ
english: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the tīrtha Saṃnihitī, where the gods headed by Brahma and the sages rich in austerity, endowed with great merit, come together month after month.

sanskrit: saṃnihityām upaspṛśya rāhugraste divākare aśvamedhaśataṃ tena iṣṭaṃ bhavati śāśvatam
english: Touching the waters of Saṃnihitī when the sun is seized by Rāhu, one has the eternal merit of a hundred Aśvamedha sacrifices performed.

sanskrit: pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni antarikṣacarāṇi ca nadyo nadās taḍāgāś ca sarvaprasravaṇāni ca
english: Whatever tīrthas there are on earth and those that move through the sky, rivers large and small, lakes and all springs —

sanskrit: udapānāś ca vaprāś ca puṇyāny āyatanāni ca māsi māsi samāyānti saṃnihityāṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: — wells and embankments, and all the holy sanctuaries — they all come to Saṃnihitī month after month — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yat kiṃ cid duṣkṛtaṃ karma striyā vā puruṣasya vā snātamātrasya tat sarvaṃ naśyate nātra saṃśayaḥ padmavarṇena yānena brahmalokaṃ sa gacchati
english: Whatever evil deed has been done by a woman or a man — all of that perishes for one who has merely bathed there, there is no doubt, and one goes to the world of Brahma in a vehicle the colour of a lotus.

sanskrit: abhivādya tato yakṣaṃ dvārapālam arantukam koṭirūpam upaspṛśya labhed bahu suvarṇakam
english: Having paid reverence to the Yakṣa, the doorkeeper Arantuka, and having touched the form of Koṭi, one obtains much gold.

sanskrit: gaṅgāhradaś ca tatraiva tīrthaṃ bharatasattama tatra snātas tu dharmajña brahmacārī samāhitaḥ rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ phalaṃ vindati śāśvatam
english: And there too is the pool of the Gaṅgā, a tīrtha, O best of the Bharatas; one who has bathed there, O knower of dharma, as a celibate with a collected mind, obtains the eternal merit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices.

sanskrit: pṛthivyāṃ naimiṣaṃ puṇyam antarikṣe ca puṣkaram trayāṇām api lokānāṃ kurukṣetraṃ viśiṣyate
english: Naimiṣa is holy on earth, and Puṣkara in the sky, but Kurukṣetra is distinguished among all three worlds.

sanskrit: pāṃsavo 'pi kurukṣetre vāyunā samudīritāḥ api duṣkṛtakarmāṇaṃ nayanti paramāṃ gatim
english: Even the dust of Kurukṣetra, stirred up by the wind, leads even one of evil deeds to the highest state.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇena sarasvatyā uttareṇa dṛṣadvatīm ye vasanti kurukṣetre te vasanti triviṣṭape
english: Those who dwell in Kurukṣetra, to the south of Sarasvatī and to the north of Dṛṣadvatī, dwell in heaven.

sanskrit: kurukṣetraṃ gamiṣyāmi kurukṣetre vasāmy aham apy ekāṃ vācam utsṛjya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: 'I will go to Kurukṣetra,' 'I dwell at Kurukṣetra' — even uttering one such word, one is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: brahmavedī kurukṣetraṃ puṇyaṃ brahmarṣisevitam tadāvasanti ye rājan na te śocyāḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Kurukṣetra, the altar of Brahma, holy, frequented by brahmin-sages — those who dwell there, O king, are not to be pitied in any way.

sanskrit: tarantukārantukayor yad antaraṃ; rāmahradānāṃ ca macakrukasya etat kurukṣetrasamantapañcakaṃ; pitāmahasyottaravedir ucyate
english: What lies between Tarantuka and Arantuka, and the lakes of Rāma and Macakruka — this Kurukṣetra-Samantapañcaka is called the northern altar of the Grandfather.

sanskrit: pulastya uvāca tato gaccheta dharmajña dharmatīrthaṃ purātanam tatra snātvā naro rājan dharmaśīlaḥ samāhitaḥ āsaptamaṃ kulaṃ rājan punīte nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Pulastya said: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the ancient tīrtha Dharmatīrtha; a man who bathes there, O king, virtuous in conduct and with a collected mind, purifies his family to the seventh generation, O king — there is no doubt.
